changes: Cleared cold_hardy yes: Wikipedia only says the breed adapts to most conditions, which does not state cold hardiness. Added hen 2.5 kg, rooster 3.5 kg and egg_color creamy white from the Wikipedia infobox values already stored in breeds.json (3.5 kg, 2.5 kg, white cream). Confirmed up to 200 eggs a year, dual purpose and French origin. FAO DAD-IS (France) confirms French origin from a local breed crossed with Columbian Brahma at the end of the 19th century, lists meat as the main use and describes a semi-heavy, long-legged bird. No second publisher for egg or weight figures, so needs_review stays true.

summary.value: The Bourbonnaise is a French farm chicken from the old province of Bourbonnais in central France. White poultry had been kept there for a long time, and crossing those local birds with Columbian Brahmas near the end of the 1800s produced the Bourbonnaise, a white bird with dark markings like the Brahma. It is a semi heavy breed with fairly long legs. Cocks weigh about 7.7 pounds and hens about 5.5 pounds. It is a practical dual purpose bird: hens lay up to 200 cream colored eggs a year, and the young grow fast, reaching adult size by about six months. The birds are vigorous, forage well and look after themselves, yet they also cope with life in a coop. That mix of hardiness and productivity makes the breed a good choice for small farms and backyard keepers, and it is listed on the Slow Food Ark of Taste.
